mainText:
The Black Caps have fought to a draw against India in Wellington, closing on nineteen past the century mark for two wickets after India declared on seven hundred and twenty for nine.

New Zealand.

The Black Caps battled through day five at the Basin Reserve to save the first test against India. New Zealand closed on one hundred and nineteen for two after India's declaration on seven hundred and twenty for nine, the highest total ever scored against New Zealand. Captain Tom Latham's side now turn to the second test.

Police are appealing for help to find Auckland man Zeal Rakei, missing since the evening of the nineteenth of November from Beach Haven on the North Shore. Police and family hold concerns for his welfare and say he may be heading towards Hastings or Gisborne.

National MP Nicola Grigg is taking medical leave after a cancer diagnosis. Christopher Luxon says her prognosis is positive but she has further treatment ahead. Grigg remains an MP while she receives care.

Fonterra has applied for permission to discharge millions of litres of raw milk, saying processing constraints mean it needs a back up option this season. The dairy giant says it has managed to process all its milk so far. The resource consent application is now before regulators.

NZ First MP Michael Laws is still refusing calls to quit Parliament after mocking an Opportunity Party opponent's appearance. A person familiar with the party's processes says the coalition's two seat majority means it is effectively stuck with him. Winston Peters has not acted.

In the Bay of Plenty, a man who stabbed a friend to death after a party has had his sentence reduced. Dallas Hohua may now serve as little as two years for the manslaughter.

World.

Rwanda backed rebels have entered Goma in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Congolese troops were overrun amid gunfire and shelling, and the United Nations estimates more than one million displaced people are now inside the city. Fighting is ongoing.

The COP thirty one climate talks have collapsed without a deal in Turkiye, the longest running summit in its history and the first outright failure since two thousand and nine. Negotiations broke down over whether to mention fossil fuels at all. There is no date yet for when talks might resume.

A suspected drone attack has caused an explosion on a Russian ship docked at Libya's Benghazi naval base. The vessel was returning to Russia after stopping for fuel and supplies. No country has claimed responsibility.

Christopher Luxon has called Vladimir Putin a killer, after Donald Trump met the Russian president at the APEC summit in China and described him as a friend. Luxon made the comments in a studio interview, sharpening his criticism of the US president's stance towards Moscow.

Technology.

Tech stocks have fallen sharply, with Anthropic shares sliding as part of a broader sell off that has pushed US markets further into correction territory. Anthropic listed last week after raising eighty one billion US dollars, the first purely AI company to go public. A Kiwi fund manager says the scale of ongoing compute spending leaves no room for error.

Caution is being urged after another major travel booking site was hacked. Bookit, Booking.com and now Expedia have each confirmed data breaches in recent months. Travellers are advised to watch for suspicious contact referencing real bookings.

Sport.

Rugby. All Blacks selector Sir Graham Henry says the team ran out of gas against England, backing coach Dave Rennie after back to back defeats to Wales and England. New Zealand Rugby boss Steve Lancaster says Rennie has the organisation's full support. Fiji, Samoa and Tonga all won their weekend internationals, Fiji claiming its first win of the series.

Football. Manchester United were thrashed four nil by Liverpool at Anfield, reduced to ten men after an eighth minute red card to Leny Yoro. It is Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge and United's worst result under a new manager in a century. They remain in the Premier League relegation zone.

Formula One. Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix featuring thirty four lead changes and a collision between the two Ferraris. Verstappen afterwards said championship rival George Russell was, in his words, so far below his level.

Tennis. Carlos Alcaraz beat world number one Alexander Zverev to win his first ATP Finals title in Turin.

Sailing. The Black Foils won in Dubai, a victory the crew said put a difficult SailGP season behind them.

Motorsport. A competitor was killed in a crash during a motorsport event in Whanganui. MotorSport New Zealand's president says the community is shocked by the tragedy. No further detail has been released.

Coming up. New Zealand Rugby faces continued questions this week over Dave Rennie's position as coach. The Black Caps turn to preparation for the second test against India. Tairāwhiti remains under a Gang Conflict Warrant following recent serious incidents.

End of flash.
